Won’t Believe How These Snakes Are Born! ‼️😱 Garter snakes are some of the most common snakes you’ll find in Oregon, but their life cycle has a pretty wild beginning. Unlike many snakes, garter snakes don’t lay eggs. The females give birth to live young, sometimes producing dozens of babies at once! The newborn snakes are completely independent from the moment they’re born. There’s no nest, no feeding from mom, and basically no parental care. They immediately start hunting small prey like worms, slugs, amphibians, and other tiny animals. As temperatures drop in the fall, garter snakes become much less active and spend the cold months sheltering underground, sometimes gathering with other snakes at communal overwintering sites. When Oregon warms back up in spring, they emerge and become active again. This is also when much of their mating activity takes place, starting the cycle all over again. And if you see one in Oregon, there’s usually no reason to worry. Garter snakes are generally harmless to people and play an important role as predators in our local ecosystems.
